scope: Conditional number-format sections, as exercised by testing/src/r77sheet. Every conditional observation is re-derived here; the external reference cannot adjudicate them and that limitation is pinned by re-executed observations rather than asserted.

semantics.selection: Up to two bracket conditions per format. Sections are tested in source order and the first satisfied condition wins; when none is satisfied the trailing section that carries no condition is used. A condition may not follow an unconditional section, two conditions may not share a section, and a format whose every section carries a condition and matches none is refused.
semantics.sign: A section never gains an automatic minus sign; only a single-section, unconditional format auto-signs a negative value. `#,##0;#,##0` therefore hides the sign of negatives, and `#,##0;-#,##0` is the way to show it.
semantics.annotations: Colours (`[Red]`, `[Color10]`) and locale/currency annotations (`[$-409]`, `[$€-407]`) are removed as annotations; the currency symbol survives as a literal. Elapsed `[h]`/`[m]`/`[s]` tokens are not conditions.
semantics.boundaries: Condition thresholds are decimal literals; scientific notation, empty thresholds and unknown annotations are refused rather than parsed leniently.

sources: ECMA-376 Part 1 §18.8.31 (number format section grammar, sections separated by `;`, annotations in brackets).
Microsoft, "Review guidelines for customizing a number format" (sections for positive/negative/zero/text; a comma after digit placeholders scales by 1,000).
https://exceljet.net/articles/custom-number-formats (conditions `[>100]`/`[<=100]` override the positive/negative/zero structure; at most two conditions).
https://trumpexcel.com/change-negative-to-positive-in-excel/ (`#,##0;#,##0` displays negatives without a minus sign because the second section has none).

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5450120/cant-display-right-a-negative-number-in-a-custom-f (the fix for a misplaced sign is to write it into the negative section: `"=" 0.00%;"="-0.00%`).

reference.name: ssf
reference.note: Python port of SheetJS ssf, installed from PyPI into an isolated cache; no code is vendored. It is used here only for the unconditional control formats.
reference.limitation: The reference does not evaluate bracket conditions: it formats the value with a section chosen by sign, so every conditional row is outside its competence. This file pins four observations that demonstrate the limitation, and tools/check_r77_sheet_conditions.py re-executes them on every run.

reference_pinned_observations.why: The condition is false and the format has no unconditional fallback; the reference ignores the condition entirely.
The reference keeps its sign-based selection and then adds a minus in front of the section's own literal.
Coincides here, but by a different route: the reference never evaluated `[<0]`, so agreement on this row is not evidence about conditions.
Both sections render 150 for the reference because the condition is invisible to it; the row cannot distinguish the two implementations.

refused_shapes.reason: The single section is conditioned and does not match; there is no fallback to select.
Every section is conditioned and none matches.
Two conditions in one section are not defined by the grammar we implement.
Scientific-notation thresholds are not decimal literals.
Unknown annotation (not a colour, locale, elapsed token or condition).
A condition follows an unconditional section, so the unconditional section would shadow it.
Three conditions are declared; Excel defines at most two.

residual_risk: No spreadsheet application ran. The selection and sign rules are derived from ECMA-376 and from public Excel behaviour, and the reference cannot check them, so conditional formatting of real cells is specification-derived rather than verified.
